newsitem.title: UK: UK natural gas OTC market sees growth in index trade.
newsitem.headline: UK natural gas OTC market sees growth in index trade.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market is moving towards the development of a derivatives market as participants start to do more deals on an index-related basis rather than at a fixed price, traders said.
A trade was done on Tuesday at a discount to indices published by two different reporting services, with a floor price set at an absolute level.
The two indices are the Heren index, published by PH Energy Analysis, and the monthly buy/sell index published in Petroleum Argus's Argus European Natural Gas Report.

The deal, for 100,000 therms a day in the third quarter of this year, was similar to a deal done last Thursday, also at a discount to the same indices, with a floor price and also in the third quarter, for 300,000 therms a day. Most trades for a quarter are done in lots of 25,000 therms a day.

A participant in last Thursday's deal said that the floor price was put in to protect the seller in case the price of gas falls between the time the deal was struck and the time when the index price will apply.
"If the index comes in below the floor, then the floor price will prevail," the dealer said.

The trader said that such deals are becoming more common. "One or two or three companies are starting to do it. One or two company's performances, and even some personal performances, are being linked to indices. I think it's coming in."
One of the traders involved in the deal on Tuesday, when the physical market was extremely illiquid, agreed that index trade is becoming more common.
"Especially on days like this it gives you the time to look at more intricate deals rather than punting around at fixed prices," he said.

"We are looking at index trading a lot more and we have done index-related trade in the past. We're keen to see more done on an index basis. Once the index is established you'll have more derivatives and swaps. You'll see a move towards a paper market," he added.

Another trader said he had seen index trading increase, but added "we have seen it occurring but it's not by any means frequent. It is becoming more common, but do two trades make a trend? I don't think so." He added that "we would only sell at a positive to an index," expressing some surprise that players were willing to sell at a discount.
A futures broker had some reservations about the development of index trading.
"The idea (of the IPE natural gas contract) was to see trade done on the IPE, not off other indices," he said. "That certainly wouldn't help our cause."
